candidates.change_summary: Change require(msg.value == 1 ether) to require(msg.value == 0 ether).
Change guesses[msg.sender].block = block.number + 1 to guesses[msg.sender].block = block.number.
Change guesses[msg.sender].block = block.number + 1 to guesses[msg.sender].block = block.number + 2.
Change guesses[msg.sender].guess = hash to guesses[msg.sender].guess = bytes32(0).
Insert guesses[msg.sender].guess = keccak256(abi.encodePacked(hash)) before the original assignment.
Delete require(msg.value == 1 ether).
Delete require(guesses[msg.sender].block == 0).
Move require(msg.value == 1 ether) after the assignments.
Delete the require that guesses[msg.sender].block == 0 in lockInGuess.
Replace the require(msg.value == 1 ether) with require(true) in lockInGuess.
Replace the block assignment with block.number instead of block.number + 1 in lockInGuess.
Change the first require in lockInGuess so it checks that the sender's block is nonzero instead of zero.
Change the second require in lockInGuess so it checks that msg.value is not equal to 1 ether instead of equal.
Delete the first require in lockInGuess that prevents a sender from locking in more than once.
Move the assignment of the sender's block number so it occurs immediately before the second require instead of after the guess assignment.
Change the transfer amount from 2 ether to 1 ether, so the caller receives less ETH on a correct guess.
Change the balance check from 2 ether to 1 ether, causing a revert for correct guesses when contract holds less than 2 ether but at least 1 ether.
Change the blockhash lookup to use block.number instead of the guessed block, making the answer deterministic per call and altering win conditions.
Delete the require that checks block.number > guessed block, allowing settlement in the same block and making the blockhash zero.
Replace the require guard on line 25 with a tautology so a caller with no prior guess can reach settle without reverting there.
Weaken the strict block-number check to >= so settle can be called in the same block as the recorded guess block.
Derive the answer from the current block hash rather than the guessed block hash.
After the payout transfer, the recorded block is reset; move that reset from before the transfer to after it.
Remove the payout guard so a correct guess attempts a 2 ether transfer even when the contract balance is insufficient.
Pay out 1 ether instead of 2 ether on a correct guess.
Change the correct-guess comparison to inequality so any wrong guess is paid out instead.
Deleting require(guesses[msg.sender].block != 0) allows settle() to proceed for an address that never locked in a guess, avoiding the revert in that case.
Deleting the require checking block.number > guesses[msg.sender].block allows settling in the same block as lockInGuess, avoiding that revert.
Replacing the hash source with the current block hash changes which guess is accepted, making otherwise-winning calls fail and possibly reverting later.
Changing the zeroed field from block to guess leaves the block set, so a second settle call can proceed further than in the original.
Deleting the balance requirement lets a winning settle proceed even when the contract cannot pay, changing revert behavior for winning guesses.
Changing transfer to send makes the winning payout silent on failure, so a winning settle can complete instead of reverting when transfer would fail.
